lines.text: Today you will learn how phone payments work, and the safety rules that keep your family’s money safe.
UPI lets people send money from one bank account to another using a phone app.
It works in seconds, at any time of the day.
In India, people use it to pay for everything from vegetables to school fees.
A QR code is a square pattern of black and white dots.
A grown-up scans the shop’s QR code with a UPI app, and the app shows the shop’s name.
Always check the name and the amount before paying.
A debit card takes money straight from a bank account.
A credit card uses borrowed money that must be paid back later.
Both are protected by a secret PIN.
A PIN is a secret number, and an OTP is a one-time password sent by text message.
Never share them with anyone, even someone who says they are from the bank.
Real banks never ask for your PIN or OTP.
Messages like ‘You won a free phone, pay ₹99 to claim it!’ are scams.
You never need to enter a PIN to receive money, only to send it.
If something feels strange, stop and tell a grown-up.
Riya and her father are paying eighty five rupees at the kirana shop.
Papa opens his UPI app and scans the QR code on the counter.
The phone shows the shop’s name, so they check that it is the right shop, and then check the amount.
Papa types his secret PIN while hiding the screen, and the payment successful message appears.
Kabir sees this message on his mother’s phone, saying he won a free phone.
It asks for ninety nine rupees and says hurry, the offer ends in ten minutes.
Red flags: a prize he never entered, a payment for something free, and a rush.
Kabir does not click anything, and he shows the message to his mother straight away.
Rule one, never share a PIN, an OTP or a password with anyone.
Rule two, always ask a grown-up before any online payment.
Rule three, check the name and the amount before any money is sent.
Rule four, if there is a free prize, a rush or a stranger asking, stop and tell a grown-up.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
